runtime.progress_trace_limit: Snapshots never acquire the COM gate. V6 samples ordinary calls every 256 entries; critical calls and failures retain detailed state. Totals describe the last sampled completion and idle is not proof that another unsampled call is idle. Missing snapshots may mean scheduling/I/O delay or lost queued output. These are not GPU timings.
runtime.gate_waiters_limit: Instantaneous counts without wait-duration attribution; they do not quantify contention cost or prove a deadlock.

source_audit.proxy_wrap_lookup: Linearly walks the entire live guest proxy linked list under proxy_lock, comparing token and interface_id.
source_audit.proxy_release_lookup: When guest references reach zero, linearly walks the same list under proxy_lock to unlink the object.
source_audit.complexity: O(N) worst case in live guest proxies for an identity lookup or unlink.
limits: The log counts native live interface slots, not the exact number of guest proxies or the number/location of proxy_wrap hits.
Only operations that publish returned COM interfaces use proxy_wrap; it is not a scan on every draw or setter.
This establishes an avoidable algorithmic cost in the v6 implementation, not its measured share of the 3D frame time.
Identity, reference ownership, allocation failure and concurrent release behavior must stay correct in a replacement lookup.

conclusions: The native ARM64 gameplay route and v6 sampled-diagnostic marker are observed; the user independently reports improved visible playback and 16-17 FPS average.
The final four 600-interval Present windows are 17.6266, 15.3395, 17.9949 and 16.0125 FPS; pooled rate is 16.6704 FPS. Scene labels are absent.

The camera-dependent user observation is consistent with scene-dependent draw/submission and GPU work. These logs cannot assign the drop to CPU, bridge, GPU, memory bandwidth or one specific resource.

Over the selected tail interval the bridge handles about 5911 calls and 765 draws per Present and copies exactly 9 MiB per Present. Fixed-size shadow copies remain a candidate cost, without a measured bandwidth bottleneck.

The x86 guest proxy still scans live objects for returned COM interface identity and zero-reference removal. Replacing those scans and avoiding small native array heap allocations are concrete candidates, with hardware FPS impact unmeasured.
Native DXVK removes FEX translation of DXVK implementation code; the game, guest proxy, Wine guest/native transitions, Map shadow copies and GPU work remain.

The DXVK renderer records an unknown interface query warning, while no bridge unsupported/fault or device-loss event is present. The warning alone does not identify a failure or the performance cause.
The active tail has 16649 live native interface slots and no guest-process shutdown marker. This does not establish a leak or clean long-session shutdown.
No current COM result or guest log was supplied; the byte-identical old v3 runtime cannot validate a v6 COM self-test.
Comparing this user improvement or these window rates with v5/x86 is not a controlled FPS benchmark because scene, camera, clocks and cache state are unmatched.
